title: Rise, Crowned with Light, Imperial Salem, Rise
description: Rise, Crowned with Light, Imperial Salem, Rise in Tonic Solfa to LANGRAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Alexander Pope wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 298 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Predicted Glory of the Messiah's Kingdom”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Tens (10.10.10.10), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to LANGRAN; any other Tens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Rise, crowned with light, im-per-ial Sa-lem, rise! Ex-alt thy tow-ering head, and lift thine eyes! See heaven its spark-ling por-tals wide dis-play, And break up-on thee in a flood of day!

lines: Rise, crowned with light, imperial Salem, rise!
Exalt thy towering head, and lift thine eyes!
See heaven its sparkling portals wide display,
And break upon thee in a flood of day!
See a long race thy spacious courts adorn,
See future sons and daughters yet unborn,
In crowding ranks on every side arise,
Demanding life, impatient for the skies!
See barbarous nations at thy gates attend,
Walk in thy light, and in thy temples bend!
See thy bright altars thronged with prostrate kings,
While every land its joyous tribute brings.
The seas shall waste, the skies to smoke decay,
Rocks fall to dust, and mountains melt away
But fixed his word, his saving power remains,
Thy realm shall last, thy own Messiah reigns.

licence: Public domain: Alexander Pope died in 1744.
credits: Words by Alexander Pope (1688–1744), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to LANGRAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
